title: Weather and zero-shot forecasting models: backtest results for GB electricity demand (part 1 of 2)

primary_sources.paraphrase: Archived record (12 Nov 2026): three zero-shot models and a weekly-lag regression get the same ECMWF forecasts as public at issue time, for GB national demand a day ahead, over a 960-day backtest. Weather cut error for all four (34%, 32%, 23%, 6%); the models' edge over the regression largely disappears. Plan, code and inputs frozen 10 Nov 2026, before scoring.

Repository of the study series (MIT). Holds plans, locks, code and results for both studies. The first study, without weather, put Chronos-2 at 0.928 of the regression's error. Weights are downloaded at pinned revisions; the README states Chronos-2 and TimesFM 2.5 are Apache 2.0 and Timestral is under a Modified MIT licence.

Results note. Q1 (confirmatory): weather lowers every forecaster's error, ratios 0.658 to 0.941. Q3 (descriptive): with weather Chronos-2 is at 0.966 of the regression's error, Timestral 1.074, TimesFM 2.5 1.453. The regression had calendar terms the models lacked; given them too (exploratory, after publication), Chronos-2 is at 0.903.

Analysis plan frozen at tag weather-plan (10 Nov 2026), written before any forecaster was given real weather. Only Q1 is confirmatory (four tests at 0.0125 each); the comparison with the regression (Q3) is an estimate with an interval and no test. Gate checks and result sentences were fixed in advance.

Model card of the central model: 120M parameters, zero-shot, takes past-only and known-future covariates natively, runs on CPU. The repository's commit history dates the weights file to 30 Oct 2025; later commits change only the README and tags.

claims.text: Weather lowered the regression's mean daily error to 0.658 of its error without weather (confirmatory).
Weather lowered Chronos-2's mean daily error to 0.683 of its error without weather (confirmatory).
Weather lowered Timestral-209M's mean daily error to 0.773 of its error without weather (confirmatory).
Weather lowered TimesFM 2.5's mean daily error to 0.941 of its error without weather (confirmatory).
With the same weather, Chronos-2's mean daily error was 0.966 times the weekly-lag regression's, against 0.932 without weather: a rough tie (descriptive).
With the same weather, Timestral-209M's mean daily error was 1.074 times the regression's, against 0.914 without weather (descriptive).
With the same weather, TimesFM 2.5's mean daily error was 1.453 times the regression's, against 1.017 without weather (descriptive).
On the 925 days that are not bank holidays or Christmas, Chronos-2 with weather was at 0.940 of the regression's error (exploratory, added after publication).
claims.dataset: GB national demand (INDO), half-hourly, ordinary days

claims.text: Given the regression's calendar terms as well as the weather, Chronos-2's error was 0.903 times the regression's (exploratory, added after publication).
Weather closed 456 MW of Chronos-2's gap to the system operator's own day-ahead forecast, 62% of the gap; the operator still leads.
The plan, code and inputs were frozen and tagged before any model forecast demand with real weather, and the backtest was scored once.

relevance.rationale: Electric load at sub-daily resolution (GB national demand, half-hourly; ours is hourly zonal PJM load). Day-ahead, issued 09:30 the day before, against our week-ahead 168 h. Weather enters as a known-future input from archived forecasts as public at issue time, which matches our forecast regime; the study uses temperature, wind and solar where our spec requires temperature only.

checks.notes: pre_registered: the plan states it was frozen at tag weather-plan on 10 Nov 2026 and the results note says the backtest was scored once on 11 Nov; a directory listing at the release tag shows PLAN.md and the lock committed 10 Nov and the results 12 Nov. The tag's push time was not inspected, and commit dates are set by the author's machine. Only Q1 (weather helps each forecaster) was confirmatory; the tie with the regression (Q3) is a pre-specified estimate without a test; E4 and E5 were added after publication. The note reports one departure from the plan (results published before the live window ends). training_overlap_risk is about our run: the Hugging Face commit history dates the Chronos-2 weights file to 2025-10-30, before our first scored week (2025-11-10), so all 52 weeks follow it. The study's own backtest overlaps the models' possible training period, which it states; its live window reports in April 2027. independent_replication: one research call and one search found no replication or dispute; the research call named a separate benchmark (winderai/demand-forecasting-benchmark) that scores Chronos-2 and Timestral on GB demand over 28 and 5 days with another metric and baseline, known here only from the source snippet, not fetched and not a replication. Central model: Chronos-2, the best of the three models in the headline comparison and the only one whose interval reaches the regression; Timestral-209M and TimesFM 2.5 are the others. baseline_same_inputs is partly throughout Q3: weather matched, but the regression had calendar terms and a year of daily refits while the models saw eight weeks; E5 gives Chronos-2 the calendar too, yet history length still differs. Licence: Apache 2.0 for Chronos-2 comes from the study's README and from the card metadata as returned by the research call; the licence tag was not in the fetched card text. discovered_via: the lead came from the Zenodo feed listing in the Claude-provider scan of 14 Nov. The research call did not reach RESULTS.md and gave only rounded figures; exact ratios are from the fetched results note. Not verified: the contents of the Zenodo archive (only its file listing was read), results.json, the numbers against the scored outputs, and gb-weather-private (not opened).

label: ACCEPT_RUN
label_reason: On target (electric load with forecast weather as a known-future input, against a lag regression given the same weather), with a public record, plan, code and results, and its headline comparison can be re-measured now with Chronos-2, which is in runnable_models. Evidence is moderate rather than strong because the tie with the regression is a descriptive estimate, not the confirmatory test, the regression had calendar terms the models did not, and nobody independent has replicated it.
implementation_hint: Chronos-2 with temperature through models/chronos2.py (weights amazon/chronos-2, direct_adapter) against the temperature-only regression, forecast regime, per zone: this is the protocol's primary comparison. Secondary rows for the study's other models: mistralai/Timestral-209M with temperature and google/timesfm-2.5-200m-pytorch univariate, both through models_ff/run_ff.py. The study pinned amazon/chronos-2 at 29ec376 and used half-hourly data, an eight-week context and three weather variables; ours is hourly, 168 h ahead, temperature only.

receipt.claimed: Given the same forecast weather, Chronos-2's mean daily error was 0.966 times a weekly-lag regression's (90% range 0.931 to 1.001) on GB national demand, day-ahead, over 960 days: a rough tie, where without weather the model led at 0.932.
receipt.horizon_mismatch: The study is GB national demand, half-hourly, day-ahead, with temperature, wind and solar forecasts, an eight-week model context and a regression with calendar terms refit daily on a year of data; ours is PJM zonal load (JC, DOM), hourly, week-ahead (168 h), temperature only, against the temperature-only regression, forecast regime. Same Chronos-2 weights revision (29ec376).
